title: Verifier‑Augmented LLM for Intent→Configuration Safety (Repaired Preregistration)
research_question: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM-driven intent→configuration loop reduce the proportion of unsafe/configurations that fail deterministic validation compared to an LLM-only single-pass baseline on a 300-task synthetic, mixed-vendor NetOps task suite?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H0: Verifier-augmentation does not change the proportion of tasks that achieve a final verifier-pass within the prespecified repair budget versus LLM-only.
H1: Verifier-augmentation (generate→verify→repair loop, ≤2 repairs) produces a ≥30% relative reduction in verifier-failure proportion versus LLM-only on the prespecified task set.
exploratory_questions: Q1: How many repair iterations are typically required to reach verifier-pass?
Q2: Which verifier-assertion categories account for remaining unsafe failures after repairs?
Q3: How sensitive are primary outcomes to one alternate prompt template and to an alternate hosted LLM (subset ablations)?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic task suite of 300 intent→target-state tasks
Three vendor-CLI families: Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, Arista EOS (synthetic templates)
10 synthetic topologies (30 tasks per topology), CPU-executable deterministic verifiers and reachability simulators
model_scope: Primary: hosted LLM API (single model identifier to be recorded at execution time and logged immutably)
Alternate-ablation: different hosted LLM API (subset ablations; model identifier recorded)
All model calls limited by capability_manifest max planned_model_calls (10000)
transformation_scope: Verifier-guided repair insertion (LLM ingests verifier failure assertions as prompt context)
primary_estimand: Per-task proportion of tasks with final verifier-pass within the repair budget (binary: pass/fail), averaged across the 300 prespecified tasks (paired comparison between pipelines).
secondary_estimands: Mean model calls per task among tasks that reach verifier-pass
Distribution of remaining failing assertion categories
sampling_plan: Construct 300 confirmatory tasks: generate 10 synthetic topologies (varied sizes/connectivity) via internal topology generator; per topology sample 30 intent→target-state tasks equally across three vendor-CLI families (100 tasks per vendor). Use fixed RNG seed stream. If a task triggers an irrecoverable technical failure, replace it (resample) to preserve 300 successful task attempts. Task_cluster_count=10; confirmatory_items=300; discovery_items=0.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired per-task verifier-pass proportion (LLM-only vs LLM+Verifier). Target effect: ≥30% relative reduction in verifier-failure proportion. Alpha=0.05 two-sided; paired McNemar primary inference; N=300 chosen to exceed conservative unpaired approximation sample-size bound (assumed baseline p0=0.50, absolute difference 0.15 → unpaired n≈170). N=300 provides >0.8 power under stated assumptions; sensitivity analyses for p0∈{0.30,0.40,0.60} and paired-exact-power reported post-hoc.
exclusion_rules: If primary verifier fails to parse config: run automatic syntax-normalizer up to 1 sanitizer pass; if still unparsable => exclude task and resample replacement (no human intervention).
If deterministic verifier crashes (parser/runtime) and sanitizer cannot recover => mark excluded and resample.
If a task triggers irrecoverable technical failure (model/API/provider/infrastructure) after allowed retries => mark technical failure and resample to preserve N=300.
missingness_plan: Per-task wall-time timeout = 5 minutes. Per-model-call timeout = provider default or 120 seconds, whichever is smaller. Retry policy: for transient infrastructure/model API failures allow up to 2 automatic retries per model call with exponential backoff. Verifier parser errors: automatic sanitizer attempt up to 1 pass; if still failing mark excluded and resample. All exclusions, retries, and replacements logged and hashed; confirmatory N=300 maintained via deterministic resampling policy.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory test: paired McNemar test on per-task final pass/fail (LLM-only vs LLM+Verifier) two-sided alpha=0.05; report risk difference with 95% Wilson CIs. For model-call counts use paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test; report median and IQR. Provide failure-mode taxonomy counts, per-assertion-type breakdown, time-to-pass descriptive stats, and paired discordant-pair counts. Preserve pairing by running both pipelines on each task. All analysis code, seeds, raw outputs, and verifier logs recorded with immutable hashes.
multiplicity_plan: Primary inference is the single prespecified estimand (McNemar). Secondary endpoints are exploratory; report raw p-values and 95% CIs. Any additional/post-hoc hypothesis tests labeled exploratory; where multiple exploratory tests are summarized provide Benjamini–Hochberg FDR-adjusted q-values for context.
contamination_plan: Benchmark names: Synthetic Intent→Configuration Task Suite (this study). Risk factors: possible training-data leakage in hosted LLMs (unknown), task-sampling overlap if seeds misused, verifier incompleteness (false negatives). Detection procedures: log and hash all prompts and outputs; flag verbatim matches; maintain held-out ground-truth set of 30 tasks with canonical configs and run both verifiers; run secondary verifier/simulator on 10% audit sample of passing configs to detect cross-verifier disagreement. Item-flagging rules: cross-verifier disagreement => 'residual_uncertainty'; exact matches to canonical configs for different tasks => 'potential_contamination'. Analysis treatment: report counts of flagged items; primary analysis uses verifier-pass labels; sensitivity analyses exclude flagged items and report effect-size differences.
stopping_rule: Per-task wall-time timeout = 5 minutes. Per-model-call timeout = provider default or 120s, whichever is smaller. Model-call transient failures: up to 2 automatic retries per call (exponential backoff). Verifier repair budget: ≤2 LLM repair iterations per task; after budget exhausted mark final status=FAIL. If infrastructure provider enforces hard limits causing run interruption, stop and record progress; resume only per the frozen retry policy and record restart metadata.
planned_outputs: raw experiment artifacts (prompts, model outputs, verifier logs)
